properties.name: heal.rs gains the dangling_reference rule and de-duplicates the zero-degree arm
properties.rationale:
Recorded before the edit rather than after, so the snapshot catches the code as it stands.

THE FIX IS AT THE ROOT AND NOT BESIDE IT. The tempting repair was to widen the zero-degree rule's escape clause so a dangling pointer survives the degree check. That would have left dangling-reference detection as a side effect of a rule about attachment, which is the actual cause: `orphan_node` fires only when a subject "resolves to no node AND it carries no edge either", so the conjunction — not the coverage — is the defect. A rule that owns one thing can be reasoned about; a side effect cannot.

WHY IT IS SELF-LIMITING, which is the property worth having: population is the count of declared node-reference VALUES walked. A schema declaring no `node_ref` property gives `examined: 0`, and the sweep's existing `coverage_note` then says in words that this rule had nothing to examine — so a clean result can never be read as a clean design. That is `loop_status` refusing an unknown contributor_id, applied to a detector.

PARKING DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SUPPRESS IT, and the reason is not an oversight to be corrected later. A `GOVERNED_BY ruling: parks` says a node is deliberately attached to NOTHING, which is a statement about attachment. A pointer that resolves to nothing is not a deliberate state anybody can hold — the design cannot decide that a record is about a node it does not have. Letting the park quiet it would make the one rule that finds broken references suppressible by an unrelated ruling.

NOT MECHANICALLY REPAIRABLE, and it belongs in `repair_is_a_judgement` for a reason this session can attest to: repointing the four bad capability references this morning took reading each fact and confirming the target owned what the fact was about, and one was settled only by a VERIFIES edge rather than by any resemblance in the words. A tool guessing the target would fabricate the same class of false record the rule exists to find.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Adding a `dangling_reference` HEAL rule that walks every property the schema declares `node_ref` and reports a value resolving to no node — on its own terms, whatever the node's degree. Closes `fact:a-dangling-reference-is-only-detected-when-the-node-is-also-edgeless`, measured this morning: 7 of 9 dangling references on this graph surfaced and 2 did not, and the 2 invisible ones were exactly the 2 that carried edges. Reuses `declared_node_refs` — already documented as "THE ONLY READER of `node_ref` IN THE CRATE" — so the detector cannot come to disagree with the write-time guard about what counts as a reference. Also de-duplicates against the existing zero-degree rule, whose TemporalFact/Snapshot arm currently reports "points at nothing that exists AND it carries no edge either": that arm conflates a broken pointer with an unattached node, and once the new rule owns the pointer case, reporting both would be the same defect twice in two vocabularies — the exact noise that made a field reporter stop work (BL-176).
